```{r setup, include=FALSE}

knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
set.seed(123)   # reproducibility
```

# 1. Load packages

```{r packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(janitor)
library(skimr)
library(naniar)
library(corrplot)
library(caret)
library(randomForest)
library(e1071)
library(pROC)
```

# 2. Import data

```{r import}
raw <- read_excel("data/dataset-uci.xlsx")
dim(raw)
```

# 3. Data cleaning

## 3.1 Standardise names and convert variable types

```{r clean-and-types}
df <- raw |>
  clean_names() |>
  mutate(
    # Target: per UCI documentation 0 = gallstones present, 1 = absent
    gallstone_status = factor(gallstone_status, levels = c(0, 1),
                              labels = c("Gallstone", "No_gallstone")),
    gender = factor(gender, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("Male", "Female")),
    across(c(coronary_artery_disease_cad, hypothyroidism,
             hyperlipidemia, diabetes_mellitus_dm),
           ~ factor(.x, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes")))
  )

glimpse(df)
table(df$gallstone_status)
```
## 3.2 Quality checks

```{r quality}
# Total missing values in the whole dataset (expected: 0)
sum(is.na(df))

# Duplicate rows (expected: 0)
sum(duplicated(df))

# Summary of every variable: check the min and max of each one
summary(df)
```

## 3.3 Save the cleaned dataset

```{r save-clean}
write_csv(df, "data/gallstone_clean.csv")
```

## 3.4 Inspect suspicious values

```{r suspicious}
df |>
  mutate(row_id = row_number()) |>
  filter(obesity_percent > 150 |
         high_density_lipoprotein_hdl > 150 |
         muscle_mass_mm < 20 |
         total_body_water_tbw < 20 |
         glomerular_filtration_rate_gfr < 20 |
         low_density_lipoprotein_ldl < 30) |>
  select(row_id, age, gender, gallstone_status, weight,
         body_mass_index_bmi, obesity_percent, muscle_mass_mm,
         total_body_water_tbw, high_density_lipoprotein_hdl,
         low_density_lipoprotein_ldl, creatinine,
         glomerular_filtration_rate_gfr)
```

# 5. Statistical testing

## 5.1 Normality check

```{r normality}
num_vars <- df |> select(where(is.numeric)) |> names()

normality <- map_dfr(num_vars, function(v) {
  p_g  <- shapiro.test(df[[v]][df$gallstone_status == "Gallstone"])$p.value
  p_ng <- shapiro.test(df[[v]][df$gallstone_status == "No_gallstone"])$p.value
  tibble(variable = v, p_gallstone = p_g, p_no_gallstone = p_ng,
         normal_in_both = p_g > 0.05 & p_ng > 0.05)
})

table(normality$normal_in_both)   # TRUE = normal in both groups
```
## 5.2 Numeric variables: Wilcoxon rank-sum tests

```{r wilcoxon}
res_num <- map_dfr(num_vars, function(v) {
  x <- df[[v]][df$gallstone_status == "Gallstone"]
  y <- df[[v]][df$gallstone_status == "No_gallstone"]
  w <- wilcox.test(x, y, exact = FALSE)

  tibble(
    variable            = v,
    test                = "Wilcoxon",
    summary_gallstone   = round(median(x), 2),      # median
    summary_no_gallstone = round(median(y), 2),     # median
    # AUC = probability that a random gallstone patient has a higher value
    # than a random non-gallstone patient (0.5 = no difference)
    auc                 = unname(w$statistic) / (length(x) * length(y)),
    p_value             = w$p.value
  )
})
```
## 5.3 Categorical variables: Fisher's exact tests

```{r fisher}
cat_vars <- c("gender", "coronary_artery_disease_cad", "hypothyroidism",
              "hyperlipidemia", "diabetes_mellitus_dm")

res_cat <- map_dfr(cat_vars, function(v) {
  tab <- table(df[[v]], df$gallstone_status)
  # Percentage of patients in the 2nd level (Female / Yes) within each group
  pct <- function(g) round(100 * tab[2, g] / sum(tab[, g]), 1)

  tibble(
    variable             = v,
    test                 = "Fisher",
    summary_gallstone    = pct("Gallstone"),        # % Female or % Yes
    summary_no_gallstone = pct("No_gallstone"),
    auc                  = NA_real_,
    p_value              = fisher.test(tab)$p.value
  )
})
```


## 5.4 Combine results and adjust p-values

```{r combine}
results <- bind_rows(res_num, res_cat) |>
  mutate(
    p_adj = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH"),
    higher_in = case_when(
      test == "Wilcoxon" & auc > 0.5 ~ "Gallstone",
      test == "Wilcoxon" & auc < 0.5 ~ "No_gallstone",
      test == "Fisher" & summary_gallstone > summary_no_gallstone ~ "Gallstone",
      TRUE ~ "No_gallstone"),
    effect = ifelse(test == "Wilcoxon", abs(2 * auc - 1), NA_real_),  # 0 to 1
    significant = p_adj < 0.05
  ) |>
  arrange(p_adj)

# How many variables are significant after correction?
sum(results$significant)

# Top 15 results
results |>
  mutate(across(c(auc, effect), ~ round(.x, 2)),
         p_value = signif(p_value, 3), p_adj = signif(p_adj, 3)) |>
  select(variable, test, summary_gallstone, summary_no_gallstone,
         higher_in, effect, p_value, p_adj) |>
  head(15)

write_csv(results, "data/statistical_test_results.csv")
```

## 5.6 Adjusted check (optional)

```{r adjusted}
top_vars <- results |> filter(test == "Wilcoxon") |> slice_head(n = 5) |> pull(variable)

map_dfr(top_vars, function(v) {
  # scale the variable so odds ratios are "per 1 SD increase"
  d <- df |> mutate(x = as.numeric(scale(.data[[v]])),
                    y = as.integer(gallstone_status == "Gallstone"))
  fit <- glm(y ~ x + age + gender, data = d, family = binomial)
  s <- summary(fit)$coefficients["x", ]
  tibble(variable = v,
         odds_ratio_per_SD = round(exp(s["Estimate"]), 2),
         p_value = signif(s["Pr(>|z|)"], 3))
})
```

# 6. Predictive modelling

## 6.1 Prepare data for modelling

```{r model-prep}
# Treat clearly impossible values as missing (NA). They are filled in with the
# median INSIDE the model pipeline (7C), so the rest of that patient is kept.
model_df <- df |>
  mutate(
    obesity_percent = ifelse(obesity_percent > 200, NA, obesity_percent),
    muscle_mass_mm  = ifelse(muscle_mass_mm < 20, NA, muscle_mass_mm)
  )

# How many values were set to NA?
colSums(is.na(model_df))[colSums(is.na(model_df)) > 0]
```
## 6.2 Train/test split

```{r split}
set.seed(123)
idx      <- createDataPartition(model_df$gallstone_status, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_df <- model_df[idx, ]
test_df  <- model_df[-idx, ]

table(train_df$gallstone_status)
table(test_df$gallstone_status)
```
## 6.3 Model training

```{r train}
# 10-fold cross-validation repeated 3 times, judged by ROC-AUC
ctrl <- trainControl(method = "repeatedcv", number = 10, repeats = 3,
                     classProbs = TRUE, summaryFunction = twoClassSummary,
                     savePredictions = "final",
                     preProcOptions = list(cutoff = 0.9))

# 1. Logistic regression (interpretable baseline).
#    "corr" removes predictors correlated above 0.9 with another one,
#    which stabilises the coefficients.
set.seed(123)
fit_glm <- train(gallstone_status ~ ., data = train_df, method = "glm",
                 family = "binomial", metric = "ROC", trControl = ctrl,
                 preProcess = c("medianImpute", "center", "scale", "corr"),
                 na.action = na.pass)

# 2. Random forest (handles non-linear effects and correlated predictors)
set.seed(123)
fit_rf <- train(gallstone_status ~ ., data = train_df, method = "rf",
                metric = "ROC", trControl = ctrl, tuneLength = 5,
                preProcess = "medianImpute", na.action = na.pass)

# 3. Support vector machine with radial kernel
set.seed(123)
fit_svm <- train(gallstone_status ~ ., data = train_df, method = "svmRadial",
                 metric = "ROC", trControl = ctrl, tuneLength = 5,
                 preProcess = c("medianImpute", "center", "scale"),
                 na.action = na.pass)

fit_glm; fit_rf; fit_svm
```
## 6.4 Cross-validation comparison

```{r cv-compare, fig.width=8, fig.height=4}
cv_res <- resamples(list(Logistic = fit_glm, RandomForest = fit_rf, SVM = fit_svm))
summary(cv_res)

bwplot(cv_res, metric = c("ROC", "Sens", "Spec"))

png("figures/11_cv_comparison.png", width = 2400, height = 1200, res = 300)
print(bwplot(cv_res, metric = c("ROC", "Sens", "Spec")))
invisible(dev.off())
```
## 6.5 Test-set evaluation

```{r test-eval}
models <- list(Logistic = fit_glm, RandomForest = fit_rf, SVM = fit_svm)

# Predicted probability of "Gallstone" for each test patient
probs <- map(models, ~ predict(.x, test_df, type = "prob",
                               na.action = na.pass)$Gallstone)

rocs <- map(probs, ~ roc(test_df$gallstone_status, .x,
                         levels = c("No_gallstone", "Gallstone"),
                         direction = "<", quiet = TRUE))

perf <- imap_dfr(probs, function(p, name) {
  pred <- factor(ifelse(p >= 0.5, "Gallstone", "No_gallstone"),
                 levels = levels(test_df$gallstone_status))
  cm <- confusionMatrix(pred, test_df$gallstone_status, positive = "Gallstone")
  ci <- ci.auc(rocs[[name]])
  tibble(model       = name,
         accuracy    = unname(cm$overall["Accuracy"]),
         sensitivity = unname(cm$byClass["Sensitivity"]),
         specificity = unname(cm$byClass["Specificity"]),
         AUC         = as.numeric(auc(rocs[[name]])),
         AUC_low95   = ci[1],
         AUC_high95  = ci[3])
}) |>
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 3)))

perf
write_csv(perf, "data/model_performance.csv")
```

```{r roc-plot, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=5.5}
p11 <- ggroc(rocs, legacy.axes = TRUE, linewidth = 1) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  labs(title = "ROC curves on the held-out test set",
       x = "1 - Specificity", y = "Sensitivity", colour = "Model")
p11
ggsave("figures/12_roc_curves.png", p11, width = 6.5, height = 5.5, dpi = 300)
```

```{r confusion}
confusionMatrix(best_pred, test_df$gallstone_status, positive = "Gallstone")
```

```{r importance, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
  transmute(variable,
            odds_ratio = round(exp(Estimate), 2),
```
